answer: Each agent could post a bond that is gradually released only as it completes useful tasks, while a random subset of its outputs is audited against independent evidence. If several identities repeat one another’s claims, an echo graph can flag their shared funding or coordination and send their bonds to review. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock up capital for every identity and risk losing it when collusion is exposed; scaling a fake reef of agents becomes costly, not free. Audits should target suspicious clusters, not mere agreement, so a broad river of legitimate agents is not punished.
